user_feedback_on_prior: Makeup remains too subtle. Preserve original person but make selected colors, intensity and placement recognizable without harsh edges or excessive drama.
reference_scope: Natural Makeup, Classic Red Lip and Cloud/Berry Lips, each on the same two reused development portraits.
causes_verified: Previous confidently detected reference-blush regions had median mask coverage0.404to0.561, attenuating pigment interiors rather than only their edges.
Adding residual pigment to warm source chroma produced orange hue drift in the stronger test.
Whole brow-to-eye support imported brow-bone shading and broad relative-lightness transfer darkened already shaded eyelids twice.

Actual source/reference equality failed on seven one-code pixels within1to2.2pixels of the warp boundary because reference smoothing read black padding. Domain-normalized smoothing fixes this regression.
changes: Full cosmetic interiors with continuous edge transitions instead of a Gaussian intensity falloff through the whole cheek.
Selected cosmetic chroma plus source fine color detail, rather than adding warm source complexion to pigment hue.
Anatomical eyelid/crease support fades before the brow bone; actual reference pigment qualifies color placement.
Actual narrow selected lash/liner strokes are handled separately from the shadow mask. No procedural new lashes.
Source local eye depth stays; only additional selected cosmetic contrast is transferred. No broad skin brightening.
Brow density increases within original support while source hair hue stays and no RGB channel can brighten.
Already prominent lipstick and original lip geometry handling remain unchanged.
Both color references are smoothed over the same valid warp domain; no padded pixels contribute cosmetic color.

comparison_metrics.metric_limit: Selected-reference aligned chroma error and edit magnitude are diagnostic proxies, not calibrated skin-tone accuracy, perceived cosmetic intensity or human realism scores. Region fixed using source labels and selected-reference red excess.

visual_review.finding: More visible reference-colored blush and eyelid pigment than the previous subtle application, with stronger selected lash detail and denser source brows. Original visible texture, geometry, expression, hair and scene remain.
visual_review.remaining: Perceived hue differs with the source lightness, especially a plum/mauve appearance on the darker portrait. Lash density/placement and brow shape are not exact selected-reference matches. Existing strong lip edges remain. Human realism and look-specific intensity acceptance are not established.
visual_review.skin_limit: Makeup areas change color and some cosmetic contrast by design. Protected source RGB is exact elsewhere; no calibrated identity or photometric accuracy score is claimed.

intermediate_evidence.reason: Visible pigment but orange hue drift and pale brow edges in inspected samples.
Selected chroma copied but brow-bone region still looked painted.
Eyelid geometry improved; first sample median color-core lightness shift minus6.94 indicated extra broad shadow.
Additional contrast handling improved; seven-pixel identical-photo padding regression then fixed.
Final source protection/reproduction checks pass; no automatic appearance acceptance.

next_gate: User appearance review against the original, selected reference and previous subtle version. Production asset/runtime integration and broader fresh-photo/style/pose/Kaggle memory and latency checks remain required. No blanket deployment readiness.
latest_feedback: Use original canvas, preserve original eyebrows and facial geometry/detail. Fix lip boundary and natural cosmetic blending; do not repeat full face generation or global intensity changes.
